subject: Post-demo: deployment & dedicated sizing clarifications
message_1_body:
Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap + a few follow-up asks to make sure we size Dedicated appropriately and confirm deployment mode options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC):

Summary from our side:
- Primary workload: real-time customer chat + occasional batch reranking for weekly search refresh.
- Desired latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for chat completions.
- Peak concurrent users (est): you mentioned ~1.2k concurrent sessions at peak.

Follow-up asks we need to size Dedicated:
1) Target TPS (requests per second) at peak and at 95th percentile. Please include breakdown by API type (chat/generation vs embeddings vs rerank).
2) Typical token mix: average request tokens / average response tokens / % of requests that are long-context (>=2k tokens).
3) Concurrency expectations per user session (do sessions stay warm with KV cache reuse?).
4) Any compliance requirement that would push toward Private (VPC/on-prem) instead of Dedicated (e.g., data residency, audit tooling).

I've attached a quick capacity workbook (tidal_capacity_workbook.xlsx) with fields you can fill; also a short sample-traffic.csv format to paste real logs into. If you can send those back, we can run a focused sizing calc and recommend GPU flavoring (A100/H100/L4 mix), concurrency configuration, and an ops playbook.

Proposed next step: if helpful, schedule a 30-min sizing call with Karthik (inference) and Marissa (CS/ops) — we can walk through the workbook and run a few scenarios.

Thanks —
Logan

Open question: For H100 vs A100 vs L4, we care mostly about cost vs throughput — H100 gives latency headroom for longer contexts but is more expensive. We lean toward a mixed approach if that helps cost.

message_3_subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment & dedicated sizing clarifications — initial sizing notes
message_3_body:
Thanks for the quick numbers, Sara — very helpful. I ran a few back-of-envelope scenarios based on the CSV and your estimates; high-level recommendations below (I'll walk through math on the call):

Key inputs used:
- Peak sustained TPS: 220 rps; 95th percentile bursts up to 350 rps
- Traffic mix: 72% chat, 20% embeddings, 8% rerank
- Avg token mix (chat): req 45, resp 200 => ~245 tokens per chat request
- KV cache hit: ~60% (reduces per-request compute for repeated contexts)

Throughput math (simplified):
- Tokens/sec at 220 rps (chat portion): 220 * 0.72 * 245 ≈ 38.9k tokens/sec
- Embeddings (20%): if avg 512-dim embed request ~80 tokens each => 220 * 0.20 * 80 ≈ 3.5k tokens/sec (different kernel path)
- Rerank small, ignored for token-heavy calc but adds concurrency needs

GPU flavor guidance:
- H100 (80GB) — best latency headroom for long-context (>=2k tokens) and highest throughput for decoder pipelines. Good fit if you expect frequent long-context hits; estimate ~1 H100 can sustain ~12–18k chat tokens/sec depending on quantization and batching.
- A100 (40/80GB) — solid all-rounder, slightly less headroom on long-context vs H100. ~1 A100 (80GB) might be ~10–14k tokens/sec.
- L4 — very cost-effective for short-context interactive chat and embeddings; lower per-card throughput but much cheaper for scale. Good for embedding-heavy or short-response volume.

Preliminary capacity recommendation (Dedicated):
- Baseline: 3 x H100-80GB instances (reserved pool) + 4 x L4 nodes for embedding offload. This gives comfortable headroom for 95th percentile bursts and allows routing of short chats/embeddings to cheaper L4 nodes when latencies allow.
- Autoscale/burst: allow +2 H100 on peak bursts (ephemeral).
- Concurrency config: set per-model concurrency target around 6–8 inference workers per H100 for chat model (tunable with batching). Use continuous batching with max batch 64 and latency cap 200ms per batch.
- KV cache: allocate ~48–64GB per H100 node for shard-local KV to keep session context hot; benefit observed on repeated session traffic (your 60% reuse number matters a lot).

Ops / SLA notes:
- VPC peering + customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated Private control plane — satisfies your SOC2/audit flow.
- We'll include token-level billing and per-route latency dashboards so you can map ops alerts to traffic hotspots.

Next steps I propose:
1) Fill the workbook with a 24h sample (the CSV you mentioned) — we can run this through our sizing tool and provide a cost/throughput matrix.
2) 30-min sizing call with Sara + DevOps tomorrow afternoon PST — I'll prepare two scenarios: H100-heavy (performance-first) and L4-mixed (cost-first).
3) If you want, we can run a short PoC on Dedicated for a 48–72 hour soak to validate p95 latency at scale before commit.

Attachment: dedicated-sizing-recs.pdf (one-pager with the above scenarios and options).

Let me know which afternoon slot works and we'll send a calendar invite.

—Karthik
